figures.caption: Figure 1: NEUROTOKEN architecture. Two EEG front-ends feed three heads. The direction-AAD spatial head reads raw EEG via a closed-form CSP+band-power pipeline (no gradient shared with the front-ends); the envelope head reconstructs the attended speech envelope and the ATTUNEFLOW head scores candidate envelopes via an integrated likelihood ratio — both backpropagate through the front-ends and so share learned features. A subject adapter rescales features and predicts a per-listener cortical-response lag. Stage 1 trains everything inside the dashed box; Stage 2 freezes it and trains ATTUNEFLOW only. Layer-by-layer specification in App. G.

Table 1: Loss terms used in each training stage of NEUROTOKEN, with the equation defining each term and the linear weight applied when summing into the total stage objective. “–” means the term is not part of that stage. Stage 1 unfreezes {fθ, gψ, hs, he, subject adapter}; Stage 2 freezes all of those and unfreezes only {vϕ, pϕ}.

Table 5: Representative AAD methods. “Cons. audio” = the model takes audio as input at inference; “Gen. env.” = produces a reconstructed envelope; “Gen. audio” = produces a waveform. †wav2vecalign [11] synthesises waveforms via a separate pre-trained vocoder applied to predicted wav2vec representations rather than producing audio directly from the brain decoder; we count this as “yes” for completeness.

Figure 2: KU Leuven per-subject AAD across the headline scoring rules: ENV-MULTI (QUADTRACK), ATTUNEFLOW, ENV-MULTI-FLOW (the z-normalised ensemble that drives most of our improvement), ENV-TRIAL-FUSED, and SPATIAL. Top: 5 s windows; bottom: 1 s windows.
Figure 3: DTU per-subject AAD across the headline scoring rules: ENV-MULTI, ATTUNEFLOW, ENV-MULTI-FLOW, ENV-TRIAL-FUSED, and SPATIAL. Top: 5 s windows; bottom: 1 s windows.
Figure 4: NJU per-subject AAD across the headline scoring rules: ENV-MULTI, ATTUNEFLOW, ENV-MULTI-FLOW, ENV-TRIAL-FUSED, and SPATIAL. Top: 5 s windows; bottom: 1 s windows.

Table 6: Summary of inference scoring rules. “Inputs” is what each rule consumes; “Train cost” is whether the rule needs anything beyond the Stage-1+Stage-2 model; “Best regime” is the deployment scenario where it dominates.

Table 9: KU Leuven LOSO S1 ablation (single fold). “Change” = ∆ vs. the D2 baseline. The per-segment envelope-multi column is bounded between 55.9 and 59.5% across every intervention we tried, a 3.6-pp spread; the trial-concatenated column saturates at 95–100 %.
Table 13: KU Leuven cross-subject 3-holdout per-window AAD accuracy (%).
Table 14: DTU cross-subject 3-holdout per-window AAD accuracy (%).
Table 15: NJU cross-subject 3-holdout per-window AAD accuracy (%).

Figure 5: Common EEG front-end fθ: a temporal-then-spatial CNN with four parallel multi-scale Conv1d branches, residual fusion gated by Squeeze–Excite, and adaptive pooling to the shared 32 Hz feature rate.

Figure 7: Subject adapter: two zero-initialised MLPs reading per-channel raw-EEG statistics emit (top) a FiLM scale–shift applied channel-wise to the fθ feature stream, and (bottom) a bounded scalar lag ∆ that temporally shifts the envelope head’s prediction.

Figure 8: Spatial head hs (CSP+BandPower): three parallel feature paths — closed-form CSP log-variance, per-channel band-power, and alpha-band asymmetries — are concatenated, BatchNormstandardised, and classified by a small MLP. CSP filters WCSP are fit on the train split and frozen.

Figure 9: Envelope head he: a residual dilated 1-D CNN over the cortical-tracking gψ stream and a linear mTRF (“backward model”) FIR over raw EEG are summed; the subject adapter’s predicted lag ∆ then shifts the resulting envelope before it is compared to the audio target.

Figure 10: ATTUNEFLOW flow head vϕ: a conditional velocity network. Inputs are the noisy envelope xt=(1−t)x0+te, the EEG conditioning c=gψ(x), and a sinusoidal embedding of the flow time t. Output is the predicted velocity along the rectified-flow path. Eight residual blocks of two dilated Conv1ds each give a ∼780 ms per-block receptive field; the output projection is zero-initialised so the velocity field starts as the identity transport.

Figure 11: ATTUNEFLOW contrastive projector pϕ: two parallel MLP towers map temporally pooled (8 bins) EEG conditioning and a candidate envelope into a shared 128-d L2-normalised embedding space, scored by InfoNCE during Stage 2.
